doc.title: John Best interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998

title: Recording sessions and pay without residuals
summary: Three-hour sessions, overtime rates and no residuals.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: When you’d go to do a recording session with Glenn or even with Artie Shaw, how much time did you usually have in the studio to do a side?
Well a normal session was three hours. After that it’s overtime. Ten dollars an hour.
And how many tunes would you usually get done in three hours?
As many as they could. I think there was eventually a limit on that, but there’s been changes made. But you could do like two or three million-selling records and get ten dollars, your part.
Oh, because you didn’t get any residual or any of that kind of thing.
No. They do today, but it’s a little late for me.
